01-01.title: the shepherd
01-01.line: the LORD is my shepherd; i shall not want.
01-01.meaning: the most loved psalm starts with enough. today, notice one thing you already have that is enough.

01-02.title: modeh ani
01-02.line: i thank you, living King, for returning my soul to me with compassion.
01-02.meaning: the first words many Jews say on waking, before even getting out of bed.

01-03.title: the whole torah
01-03.line: what is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow.
01-03.meaning: Hillel's answer to a man who wanted the Torah on one foot. then he added: go and learn.

01-04.title: in the beginning
01-04.line: in the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
01-04.meaning: the Torah's first word is bereshit. every day is a small beginning too.

01-05.title: a season
01-05.line: to every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.
01-05.meaning: whatever season you're in, it has its purpose.

01-06.title: ways of pleasantness
01-06.line: her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.
01-06.meaning: sung when the Torah returns to the ark. wisdom is meant to feel pleasant, not heavy.

01-07.title: three pillars
01-07.line: the world stands on three things: Torah, prayer, and acts of kindness.
01-07.meaning: Shimon the Righteous gave a recipe for a world that holds up. which pillar is yours today?

01-08.title: still waters
01-08.line: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
01-08.meaning: rest is part of the path, not a break from it. find one quiet minute of still water today.

01-09.title: a pure soul
01-09.line: my God, the soul you gave me is pure.
01-09.meaning: Elohai Neshamah: the day starts with a clean slate.

01-10.title: a whole world
01-10.line: whoever saves a single life is as if they saved an entire world.
01-10.meaning: every one person is a whole world. treat today's people that way.

01-11.title: through the valley
01-11.line: though i walk through the valley of the shadow of death, i will fear no evil.
01-11.meaning: the psalm doesn't skip the valley. it says you won't walk it alone.

01-12.title: evening, then morning
01-12.line: and there was evening and there was morning, one day.
01-12.meaning: that's why a Jewish day starts at sunset. rest comes first, then work.

01-13.title: time to dance
01-13.line: a time to mourn, and a time to dance.
01-13.meaning: both are part of a full life. let today be what it is.

01-14.title: a tree of life
01-14.line: she is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her.
01-14.meaning: the Torah is called a tree of life. hold on, and it holds you up.

01-15.title: an open house
01-15.line: let your house be open wide.
01-15.meaning: Yose ben Yochanan pictured a home with the door open to anyone in need.

01-16.title: shehecheyanu
01-16.line: blessed are you... who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this moment.
01-16.meaning: said for firsts: new fruit, new season, big days. find a first today.

01-17.title: goodness follows
01-17.line: surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life.
01-17.meaning: goodness isn't only ahead of you. the psalm says it's following you, catching up.

01-18.title: made for my sake
01-18.line: each person must say: the world was created for my sake.
01-18.meaning: not arrogance, but responsibility. you matter enough to make a difference.

01-19.title: in God's image
01-19.line: God created man in his own image.
01-19.meaning: b'tzelem Elohim: every face you see today carries something holy.

01-20.title: my light
01-20.line: the LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall i fear?
01-20.meaning: said every day in the weeks before the High Holidays. light first, then courage.

01-21.title: beautiful in time
01-21.line: he hath made every thing beautiful in its time.
01-21.meaning: some beauty only shows up later. give it time.

01-22.title: hamotzi
01-22.line: blessed are you... who brings forth bread from the earth.
01-22.meaning: said over bread. a thank-you for the farmer, the baker, and the grain.

01-23.title: lean less
01-23.line: trust in the LORD with all thy heart, and lean not upon thine own understanding.
01-23.meaning: you don't have to figure everything out today.

01-24.title: teacher and friend
01-24.line: make for yourself a teacher, and acquire for yourself a friend.
01-24.meaning: both take effort. both are worth it.

01-25.title: take courage
01-25.line: wait for the LORD; be strong, and let thy heart take courage.
01-25.meaning: waiting can be brave. a steady heart is its own kind of strength today.

01-26.title: no two alike
01-26.line: God stamped every person from one mold, and none is like another.
01-26.meaning: a king's coins all look alike; people never do. you're one of a kind on purpose.

01-27.title: fruit of the tree
01-27.line: blessed are you... who creates the fruit of the tree.
01-27.meaning: borei pri ha'etz: one breath of thanks before a bite of fruit.

01-28.title: the seventh day
01-28.line: God blessed the seventh day, and hallowed it.
01-28.meaning: rest was the first thing ever called holy.

01-29.title: two are better
01-29.meaning: we're not built to do life solo.

01-30.title: one thing
01-30.line: one thing have i asked: to behold the graciousness of the LORD.
01-30.meaning: out of everything one could ask for, the psalmist asks to notice beauty. a good prayer for a busy day.

01-31.title: i don't know
01-31.line: teach your tongue to say 'i do not know.'
01-31.meaning: the Talmud praises honest not-knowing. it opens the door to learning.

02-01.title: don't hold back good
02-01.line: withhold not good... when it is in thy power to do it.
02-01.meaning: if you can help someone today, that's the moment.

02-02.title: the benefit of the doubt
02-02.meaning: dan l'chaf zechut: tip the scale toward kindness when you're not sure.

02-03.title: for the rainbow
02-03.line: blessed are you... who remembers the covenant.
02-03.meaning: there's a blessing just for rainbows. look up after rain.

02-04.title: always before me
02-04.line: i have set the LORD always before me.
02-04.meaning: many synagogues hang this verse above the ark. it's a way of saying: i remember who i'm standing before.

02-05.title: the breath of life
02-05.line: and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.
02-05.meaning: each breath is a small gift. take a slow one now.

02-06.title: lift your fellow
02-06.line: if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow.
02-06.meaning: be the one who helps someone up today.

02-07.title: fulness of joy
02-07.line: in thy presence is fulness of joy.
02-07.meaning: joy here isn't a reward for later. it comes from closeness, right now.

02-08.title: the carob tree
02-08.line: just as my ancestors planted for me, so i plant for my children.
02-08.meaning: Honi met an old man planting a tree that would take seventy years. we all eat from someone's planting.

02-09.title: for thunder
02-09.line: blessed are you... whose strength and might fill the world.
02-09.meaning: even a storm has a blessing.

02-10.title: guard your heart
02-10.line: keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
02-10.meaning: what you let into your heart shapes everything that comes out of it.

02-11.title: students of aaron
02-11.line: love peace and pursue peace; love people and bring them close.
02-11.meaning: Hillel's picture of Aaron, the peacemaker brother of Moses.

02-12.title: the sky is talking
02-12.line: the heavens declare the glory of God.
02-12.meaning: look up once today. the sky has been saying something all along, without a single word.

02-13.title: to work and to keep
02-13.line: put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.
02-13.meaning: our first job: tend the world and protect it.

02-14.title: threefold cord
02-14.line: a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
02-14.meaning: often read at Jewish weddings: two people, held together by something more.

02-15.title: for mountains and lightning
02-15.line: blessed are you... who makes the works of creation.
02-15.meaning: said on seeing lightning, high mountains, or a vast desert.

02-16.title: companions
02-16.line: give me companions, or what is life?
02-16.meaning: after Honi's long sleep, no one knew him. the Talmud says: either friendship or death. reach out today.

02-17.title: words of my mouth
02-17.line: let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before thee.
02-17.meaning: said quietly at the end of the Amidah. a good wish for every conversation today.

02-18.title: more and more light
02-18.line: the path of the righteous is as the light of dawn, that shineth more and more.
02-18.meaning: growth is gradual, like sunrise. you don't need to be noon yet.

02-19.title: not alone
02-19.line: it is not good that the man should be alone.
02-19.meaning: the first 'not good' in the Torah is loneliness. reach out to someone.

02-20.title: for the ocean
02-20.line: blessed are you... who made the great sea.
02-20.meaning: said on seeing the ocean after a long time away.

02-21.title: the earth's owner
02-21.line: the earth is the LORD's, and the fulness thereof.
02-21.meaning: everything we hold is on loan. that makes it easier to share, and to care for it.

02-22.title: if not now, when?
02-22.line: if i am not for myself, who will be for me?
02-22.meaning: Hillel asks two more: if i am only for myself, what am i? and if not now, when?

02-23.title: the reed
02-23.line: a person should always be soft like a reed, not hard like a cedar.
02-23.meaning: reeds bend in the wind and spring back. cedars snap.

02-24.title: eat with joy
02-24.line: go thy way, eat thy bread with joy.
02-24.meaning: Ecclesiastes, the gloomiest book, still says: enjoy your bread.

02-25.title: joy in the morning
02-25.line: weeping may tarry for the night, but joy cometh in the morning.
02-25.meaning: the night is real, and so is the morning. both are part of the same psalm.

02-26.title: good news
02-26.line: blessed are you... who is good and does good.
02-26.meaning: hatov v'hameitiv: a blessing for good news shared with others.

02-27.title: my brother's keeper
02-27.meaning: the Torah leaves the question hanging. the rest of the Torah answers: yes.

02-28.title: the ant
02-28.line: go to the ant... consider her ways, and be wise.
02-28.meaning: small, steady, together. the ant has been teaching patience for three thousand years.

02-29.title: this too
02-29.line: this too is for the good.
02-29.meaning: Nachum of Gamzu said it about everything, even the hard things. the sages called him Gam Zu.

03-01.title: mourning into dancing
03-01.line: thou hast turned my mourning into dancing.
03-01.meaning: sorrow is not the last word. sometimes the turn comes slowly, then all at once.

03-02.title: with your might
03-02.line: whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.
03-02.meaning: pick one task today and give it your whole self.

03-03.title: say little, do much
03-03.line: say little and do much, and receive everyone with a cheerful face.
03-03.meaning: Shammai, known as strict, taught this warm line about welcome.

03-04.title: the body
03-04.line: blessed are you... who formed the human body with wisdom.
03-04.meaning: Asher Yatzar: a thank-you for the ordinary wonder of a working body.

03-05.title: pursue peace
03-05.line: depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.
03-05.meaning: the sages noticed: peace isn't only sought, it's chased. go after it a little today.

03-06.title: seedtime and harvest
03-06.line: seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall not cease.
03-06.meaning: after the flood, a promise of rhythm. seasons keep coming.

03-07.title: beruriah's prayer
03-07.line: pray that the sins end, not the sinners.
03-07.meaning: Beruriah taught her husband, Rabbi Meir, to pray for people to change, not to be gone.

03-08.title: love covers
03-08.line: hatred stirreth up strifes; but love covereth all transgressions.
03-08.meaning: love doesn't keep score. let one small thing go today.

03-09.title: for a wise person
03-09.line: blessed are you... who gave of your wisdom to flesh and blood.
03-09.meaning: there's a blessing for meeting a great scholar. wisdom is worth celebrating.
03-09.source: blessing on seeing a wise person

03-10.title: bread on the waters
03-10.line: cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.
03-10.meaning: give without knowing how it returns. it often does.

03-11.title: near the broken
03-11.line: the LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart.
03-11.meaning: if your heart is cracked today, the psalm says that's exactly where closeness lives.

03-12.title: deeds over words
03-12.line: not study but doing is the main thing.
03-12.meaning: learning matters most when it turns into action.

03-13.title: guard the tongue
03-13.line: keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile.
03-13.meaning: the psalm asks who wants a good life, then answers: watch your words. a small, daily practice.

03-14.title: welcome guests
03-14.line: welcoming guests is greater than receiving the Divine Presence.
03-14.meaning: Abraham left a vision of God to greet three strangers. the sages learned: people first.

03-15.title: be a blessing
03-15.meaning: Abraham is told to go, and also to be a blessing. both start with one step.

03-16.title: the traveler's prayer
03-16.line: may it be your will to lead us in peace.
03-16.meaning: Tefillat HaDerech, said at the start of a journey.

03-17.title: sow in the morning
03-17.line: in the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand.
03-17.meaning: you don't know which seeds will grow. keep planting.

03-18.title: the one who waters
03-18.line: he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
03-18.meaning: giving refreshes the giver. pour into someone today.

03-19.title: do good, dwell
03-19.line: trust in the LORD, and do good; dwell in the land, and cherish faithfulness.
03-19.meaning: no grand plan needed: trust, do the next good thing, stay faithful where you are.

03-20.title: the value of silence
03-20.line: i found nothing better for a person than silence.
03-20.meaning: Shimon, son of Rabban Gamliel, grew up among sages and learned to listen.

03-21.title: responsible for each other
03-21.line: all Israel are responsible for one another.
03-21.meaning: no one is on their own. we're tied together.

03-22.title: who opens eyes
03-22.line: blessed are you... who opens the eyes of the blind.
03-22.meaning: part of the morning blessings. noticing the gift of sight, one blink at a time.

03-23.title: where he is
03-23.line: God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is.
03-23.meaning: Ishmael is heard as he is, where he is. you don't need to be somewhere else first.

03-24.title: roll it over
03-24.line: commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him.
03-24.meaning: the Hebrew means to roll your way onto God. hand over one worry today.

03-25.title: better the end
03-25.line: better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof.
03-25.meaning: finishing has its own sweetness. close one small loop today.

03-26.title: a good word
03-26.line: care in the heart of a man boweth it down; but a good word maketh it glad.
03-26.meaning: you may be carrying someone's good word today. say it.

03-27.title: who lifts the bowed
03-27.line: blessed are you... who straightens those who are bent.
03-27.meaning: said while standing up straight in the morning. a small lift for the day.

03-28.title: a future for peace
03-28.line: there is a future for the man of peace.
03-28.meaning: peacemakers can feel slow. the psalm promises their work lasts.

03-29.title: kindness, start to end
03-29.line: the Torah begins with kindness and ends with kindness.
03-29.meaning: God clothes Adam and Eve at the start, and buries Moses at the end. kindness is the frame.

03-30.title: justice, truth, peace
03-30.line: the world endures on three things: justice, truth, and peace.
03-30.meaning: a second set of three pillars. maybe you can hold one up today.

03-31.title: here i am
03-31.meaning: hineni means fully present. say it to someone today with your attention.

04-01.title: refuge
04-01.line: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
04-01.meaning: a very present help: not far away, not later. right here, today.

04-02.title: sleep from my eyes
04-02.line: blessed are you... who removes sleep from my eyes.
04-02.meaning: even waking up gets a blessing.

04-03.title: good days, hard days
04-03.line: in the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider.
04-03.meaning: enjoy the good days fully. on hard ones, look a little deeper.

04-04.title: walk in god's ways
04-04.line: as God clothes the naked, visits the sick, and comforts mourners, so should you.
04-04.meaning: the way to be close to God is to do what God does.

04-05.title: be still
04-05.line: be still, and know that i am God.
04-05.meaning: sometimes knowing comes after stopping. try one still minute before the day rushes in.

04-06.title: desire fulfilled
04-06.line: hope deferred maketh the heart sick; but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
04-06.meaning: waiting is hard, and the sages knew it. when hopes come true, notice and celebrate.

04-07.title: a ladder
04-07.line: a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven.
04-07.meaning: Jacob's dream: heaven and earth are connected, and the path goes both ways.

04-08.title: reward isn't the point
04-08.line: be not like servants who serve their master for the sake of a reward.
04-08.meaning: do good because it's good, not for the prize.

04-09.title: the shema at night
04-09.line: hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one.
04-09.meaning: many say the Shema in bed, the last words of the day.

04-10.title: a clean heart
04-10.line: create me a clean heart, O God; and renew a steadfast spirit within me.
04-10.meaning: a fresh start is something you can ask for, any day of the year.

04-11.title: the earth abides
04-11.line: one generation passeth away, and another generation cometh; but the earth abideth.
04-11.meaning: you belong to a long line, on an old and patient earth.

04-12.title: the sabbath queen
04-12.line: come, let us go out to greet Shabbat the queen.
04-12.meaning: Rabbi Chanina dressed up on Friday to welcome Shabbat like royalty.

04-13.title: cast your burden
04-13.line: cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee.
04-13.meaning: you don't have to carry everything alone. name one weight and set it down.

04-14.title: the mezuzah
04-14.line: a little scroll on the doorpost, touched coming and going.
04-14.meaning: each doorway becomes a reminder of what you believe.

04-15.title: wherever you go
04-15.line: behold, i am with thee, and will keep thee whithersoever thou goest.
04-15.meaning: said to Jacob as he ran away from home. a promise for anyone starting over.

04-16.title: a soft answer
04-16.line: a soft answer turneth away wrath.
04-16.meaning: the gentlest reply is often the strongest one.

04-17.title: love work
04-17.meaning: Shemaiah's teaching opens with just two words. there's dignity in a day's work.

04-18.title: two angels
04-18.line: two angels walk a person home on Friday night.
04-18.meaning: the story behind the song Shalom Aleichem. your home is visited.

04-19.title: when i'm afraid
04-19.line: in the day that i am afraid, i will put my trust in thee.
04-19.meaning: the psalmist admits fear first. trust isn't the absence of fear; it's what you do with it.

04-20.title: light is sweet
04-20.meaning: step into the light for a minute. it's a simple sweetness.

04-21.title: the tzedakah box
04-21.meaning: many families drop coins in a box before lighting. giving comes first.

04-22.title: what are you seeking?
04-22.line: and the man asked him, saying: 'what seekest thou?'
04-22.meaning: a stranger asks lost young Joseph a simple question. ask yourself the same today.

04-23.title: thirst
04-23.meaning: that restless feeling might be a kind of thirst. the psalm gives it a name.

04-24.title: a cheerful face
04-24.line: a merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance.
04-24.meaning: joy shows. let yours be seen today.

04-25.title: an extra soul
04-25.line: on Shabbat a person is given an extra soul.
04-25.meaning: neshamah yeteirah: Shabbat makes room for more of you.

04-26.title: candle lighting
04-26.line: two candles, a circle of hands, eyes covered, a blessing.
04-26.meaning: Shabbat begins with light. some add a private prayer for their family.

04-27.title: the dust of their feet
04-27.line: sit in the dust of the feet of the wise, and drink in their words with thirst.
04-27.meaning: learn like you're thirsty. sit close to people who know more.

04-28.title: winter is past
04-28.line: for, lo, the winter is past... the flowers appear on the earth.
04-28.meaning: read at Passover. every winter ends.

04-29.title: happy are they
04-29.line: happy are they that dwell in thy house.
04-29.meaning: this line opens Ashrei, prayed three times a day. it begins with happiness, not duty.

04-30.title: to preserve life
04-30.line: be not grieved... for God did send me before you to preserve life.
04-30.meaning: Joseph finds meaning in a painful story. that takes time, and it's possible.

05-01.title: number our days
05-01.line: so teach us to number our days, that we may get us a heart of wisdom.
05-01.meaning: counting days isn't gloomy here. it's how you notice that today matters.

05-02.title: kiddush
05-02.line: a cup of wine to say: this day is holy.
05-02.meaning: Kiddush means making holy. it's said with a raised cup.

05-03.title: give me your hand
05-03.line: a prisoner cannot free himself from prison.
05-03.meaning: a great rabbi could heal others but needed a friend's hand to heal himself. ask for help.

05-04.title: who directs the steps
05-04.line: a man's heart deviseth his way; but the LORD directeth his steps.
05-04.meaning: make your plan. hold it lightly.

05-05.title: many waters
05-05.meaning: love outlasts floods. tell someone you love them.

05-06.title: the right path
05-06.line: which is the right path? whatever brings honor to you and to others.
05-06.meaning: Rabbi Judah the Prince's simple test for choices.

05-07.title: the work of our hands
05-07.line: establish thou the work of our hands.
05-07.meaning: a blessing for ordinary work. may what you build today last.

05-08.title: i will be
05-08.line: i will be what i will be.
05-08.meaning: God's name to Moses at the bush. open, unfolding, never finished.

05-09.title: havdalah
05-09.line: a braided candle, sweet spices, and wine to say goodbye to Shabbat.
05-09.meaning: the spices are to comfort the soul as Shabbat leaves.

05-10.title: a blessing for everything
05-10.line: it is forbidden to enjoy this world without a blessing.
05-10.meaning: a blessing turns a snack into a thank-you.

05-11.title: guarded ways
05-11.line: he will give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
05-11.meaning: an old line for travelers and for anyone stepping into a new day.

05-12.title: like honey
05-12.line: pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul.
05-12.meaning: kind words cost nothing and taste like honey. hand some out.

05-13.title: come away
05-13.line: rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
05-13.meaning: the sages read this as God calling to us, tenderly.

05-14.title: shalom aleichem
05-14.line: peace be upon you, angels of peace.
05-14.meaning: sung on Friday night to the angels who walk us home.

05-15.title: small mitzvot count
05-15.line: be as careful with a light mitzvah as with a weighty one.
05-15.meaning: you never know which small kindness matters most.

05-16.title: good to give thanks
05-16.line: it is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD.
05-16.meaning: this is the song for the Sabbath day. thanks first, everything else after.

05-17.title: go forward
05-17.line: speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward.
05-17.meaning: at the sea, the instruction was simple: take the next step.

05-18.title: don't shame anyone
05-18.line: whoever makes another's face go pale in public, it is as if they shed blood.
05-18.meaning: embarrassment wounds deeply. protect people's dignity today.

05-19.title: like the palm tree
05-19.line: the righteous shall flourish like the palm tree.
05-19.meaning: palms bend in storms and keep growing. goodness is meant to be flexible and strong.

05-20.title: two loaves
05-20.meaning: a memory of the double portion of manna that fell before Shabbat.

05-21.title: slow to anger
05-21.line: he that is slow to anger is better than the mighty.
05-21.meaning: real strength is the pause before you react.

05-22.title: where you go
05-22.line: whither thou goest, i will go.
05-22.meaning: Ruth's loyalty to Naomi is one of the great friendships of the Bible.

05-23.title: miriam's drum
05-23.line: Miriam... took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her.
05-23.meaning: the midrash says she packed her drum in Egypt, sure there'd be a reason to dance.

05-24.title: weighs as much as all
05-24.line: tzedakah is equal to all the other mitzvot together.
05-24.meaning: giving is that central. a coin in a box counts.

05-25.title: let us sing
05-25.line: o come, let us sing unto the LORD.
05-25.meaning: Friday night welcoming of Shabbat opens with this psalm. an invitation, not a demand.

05-26.title: stay with the community
05-26.line: do not separate yourself from the community.
05-26.meaning: Hillel's advice: stay connected, even when it's easier not to.

05-27.title: shalom
05-27.line: shalom means peace, and also whole.
05-27.meaning: peace in Hebrew is about being complete, not just quiet.

05-28.title: trees sing
05-28.line: then shall all the trees of the wood sing for joy.
05-28.meaning: the psalm imagines forests singing. step outside and listen for a minute.

05-29.title: under wings
05-29.line: under whose wings thou art come to take refuge.
05-29.meaning: Boaz blesses Ruth: you've found shelter. may you find it too.

05-30.title: at all times
05-30.line: a friend loveth at all times.
05-30.meaning: not only on easy days. check on a friend who's having a hard one.

05-31.title: greater than charity
05-31.line: acts of kindness are greater than charity.
05-31.meaning: kindness can be given with your body, to rich and poor, to living and dead.

06-01.title: holding up hands
06-01.line: and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
06-01.meaning: even Moses got tired. Aaron and Hur held his arms up. hold someone up today.

06-02.title: chesed
06-02.line: chesed: kindness that goes beyond what's required.

06-03.title: rivers clap
06-03.line: let the floods clap their hands; let the mountains sing for joy together.
06-03.meaning: all of creation in one big celebration. you're invited too.

06-04.title: in their shoes
06-04.line: do not judge your fellow until you have reached his place.
06-04.meaning: you rarely know what someone is carrying.

06-05.title: study leads to doing
06-05.line: study is great, for it leads to action.
06-05.meaning: the sages debated, and agreed: learn so you can do.

06-06.title: with gladness
06-06.line: serve the LORD with gladness; come before him with singing.
06-06.meaning: service and gladness belong together. bring a little song into today's work.

06-07.title: new every morning
06-07.line: his compassions fail not. they are new every morning.
06-07.meaning: in the saddest book of the Bible, this line still shines. today is a fresh supply.

06-08.title: tzedakah
06-08.line: tzedakah: giving, from the word for justice.
06-08.meaning: in Hebrew, giving isn't only charity. it's setting things right.

06-09.title: remember shabbat
06-09.line: remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
06-09.meaning: Shabbat is remembered all week. count down to it today.

06-10.title: the tongue's power
06-10.line: death and life are in the power of the tongue.
06-10.meaning: words can build or break. choose builders today.

06-11.title: forget not
06-11.line: bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits.
06-11.meaning: gratitude is mostly remembering. name three good things from this week.

06-12.title: be a mensch
06-12.line: where there are no people being human, strive to be one.
06-12.meaning: Hillel's line behind the word mensch. someone has to go first.

06-13.title: teshuvah
06-13.meaning: coming back is always possible. it's a turn, not a punishment.

06-14.title: water on stone
06-14.line: if soft water can hollow stone, Torah can enter my heart.
06-14.meaning: Rabbi Akiva began learning at forty after watching drips carve a rock. it's never too late.

06-15.title: ask the animals
06-15.line: ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee.
06-15.meaning: nature is a teacher. watch a bird or a dog for a minute.

06-16.title: he knows our frame
06-16.line: he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.
06-16.meaning: you're not expected to be more than human. that's a mercy, not a scolding.

06-17.title: honor your parents
06-17.line: honour thy father and thy mother.
06-17.meaning: a small call or message can be honor too.

06-18.title: pass it over
06-18.line: it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
06-18.meaning: letting something go isn't weakness. Proverbs calls it glory.

06-19.title: kavanah
06-19.line: kavanah: intention, meaning what you do.
06-19.meaning: the same words feel different when you mean them.

06-20.title: how many works
06-20.line: how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all.
06-20.meaning: one leaf, one bird, one face. the variety itself is the wonder.

06-21.title: the true hero
06-21.line: who is the mightiest? one who turns an enemy into a friend.
06-21.meaning: the bravest win is a reconciliation.

06-22.title: you don't have to finish
06-22.line: it is not your duty to finish the work, but neither are you free to stop.
06-22.meaning: Rabbi Tarfon's comfort for big tasks: do your part.

06-23.title: morning stars
06-23.line: when the morning stars sang together.
06-23.meaning: Job is shown a universe full of singing. the world is bigger than our worries.

06-24.title: the heart of a stranger
06-24.line: ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.
06-24.meaning: remembering our own hard times makes us kinder to others.

06-25.title: as long as i live
06-25.line: i will sing unto the LORD as long as i live.
06-25.meaning: a lifelong song doesn't need a good voice. just a willing one.

06-26.title: tikkun olam
06-26.meaning: from the Aleinu prayer. small fixes add up.

06-27.title: a loan to God
06-27.line: he that is gracious unto the poor lendeth unto the LORD.
06-27.meaning: generosity is pictured as a loan to God, who is good for it.

06-28.title: plant the sapling
06-28.line: if you're holding a sapling and hear the Messiah has come, plant it first.
06-28.meaning: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai: keep doing the good, ordinary thing.

06-29.title: sunrise to sunset
06-29.line: from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof.
06-29.meaning: the whole day, edge to edge, is a place for praise.

06-30.title: simcha
06-30.meaning: a wedding is a simcha. so is a good morning.

07-01.title: help with the load
07-01.line: thou shalt surely release it with him.
07-01.meaning: even the donkey of someone who hates you gets a hand with its heavy load. help first, feelings later.

07-02.title: wings like eagles
07-02.line: they that wait for the LORD shall renew their strength.
07-02.meaning: tired is not the end. strength can be renewed.

07-03.title: the day is short
07-03.line: the day is short, the work is great.
07-03.meaning: Rabbi Tarfon again. pick what matters most today.

07-04.title: heard my voice
07-04.line: i love the LORD, because he hath heard my voice.
07-04.meaning: love that begins with being heard. who could you really listen to today?

07-05.title: both are true
07-05.line: these and these are the words of the living God.
07-05.meaning: Hillel's and Shammai's schools both spoke truth. Hillel's won because they taught the other side first.

07-06.title: the lamp within
07-06.line: the spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD.
07-06.meaning: there's a light inside you that can see what's true. trust it a little today.

07-07.title: hakarat hatov
07-07.meaning: gratitude, Hebrew-style: noticing it out loud.

07-08.title: out of the narrow place
07-08.line: out of my straits i called upon the LORD; he answered me with great enlargement.
07-08.meaning: sung on festivals: from a tight place to wide-open space. a hope for anyone feeling squeezed.

07-09.title: keep shabbat
07-09.line: the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath.
07-09.meaning: sung as V'shamru on Friday night and Shabbat morning. a sign between God and the people.

07-10.title: through the waters
07-10.line: when thou passest through the waters, i will be with thee.
07-10.meaning: the promise isn't no waters. it's company in them.

07-11.title: a good heart
07-11.meaning: Rabban Yochanan asked his students for the best path. the winner: a good heart, which holds all the others.

07-12.title: enjoy the world
07-12.line: a person will give account for every permitted pleasure they saw and did not enjoy.
07-12.meaning: joy isn't a distraction from faith. taste something good today.

07-13.title: this is the day
07-13.line: this is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
07-13.meaning: not yesterday, not someday. this one.

07-14.title: bitachon
07-14.meaning: the quiet feeling that it will be okay, even if you can't see how.

07-15.title: better than offerings
07-15.line: to do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
07-15.meaning: doing right by people is the offering that counts most.

07-16.title: you shall be holy
07-16.line: ye shall be holy; for i the LORD your God am holy.
07-16.meaning: holiness here is everyday: how you treat workers, strangers, the old.

07-17.title: a lamp
07-17.line: thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
07-17.meaning: a lamp shows the next step, not the whole road. that's usually enough.

07-18.title: fear not
07-18.line: fear thou not, for i am with thee.
07-18.meaning: a short line to carry into a hard meeting or a scary call.

07-19.title: only one world
07-19.line: see my works, how lovely they are. take care not to ruin my world.
07-19.meaning: God shows Adam the trees in Eden. there's no one after us to fix it.

07-20.title: l'chaim
07-20.meaning: the toast says it all. life itself is worth raising a glass to.

07-21.title: their honor as yours
07-21.line: let your friend's honor be as dear to you as your own.
07-21.meaning: Rabbi Eliezer's take on respect: treat it like it's yours.

07-22.title: open my eyes
07-22.line: open thou mine eyes, that i may behold wondrous things.
07-22.meaning: wonder is often already here. the prayer is to see it.

07-23.title: a good name
07-23.line: a good name is rather to be chosen than great riches.
07-23.meaning: a name is built one kept promise at a time.

07-24.title: no stumbling block
07-24.line: thou shalt not curse the deaf, nor put a stumbling-block before the blind.
07-24.meaning: don't take advantage of what someone can't see or hear. including bad advice.

07-25.title: chai
07-25.line: chai means life, and adds up to 18.
07-25.meaning: that's why gifts are often given in multiples of 18.

07-26.title: kindness stays
07-26.line: the mountains may depart... but my kindness shall not depart from thee.
07-26.meaning: even mountains are less steady than this love.

07-27.title: lift your eyes
07-27.line: i will lift up mine eyes unto the mountains: from whence shall my help come?
07-27.meaning: sometimes looking up is the first step to feeling helped.

07-28.title: the runaway lamb
07-28.line: you have mercy on a lamb; you will shepherd my people.
07-28.meaning: Moses chased a thirsty lamb and carried it back. that's when God chose him.

07-29.title: for the sake of heaven
07-29.line: let all your deeds be for the sake of heaven.
07-29.meaning: Rabbi Yose: even eating and sleeping can have a holy purpose.

07-30.title: going out, coming in
07-30.line: the LORD shall guard thy going out and thy coming in.
07-30.meaning: many say this leaving home. every doorway today is held.

07-31.title: mitzvah
07-31.line: mitzvah: a commandment, and a connection.
07-31.meaning: many read it as a way of being joined to God. a good deed is a bond.

08-01.title: no gossip
08-01.line: thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer.
08-01.meaning: one less story passed along today is a real gift.

08-02.title: four open doors
08-02.line: Abraham's tent was open on all four sides.
08-02.meaning: so guests from any direction could find the way in.

08-03.title: their own way
08-03.line: train up a child in the way he should go.
08-03.meaning: the Hebrew hints 'according to his way': teach each child as the person they are.

08-04.title: trees clap
08-04.line: ye shall go out with joy... and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands.
08-04.meaning: the world applauds when we set out in joy.

08-05.title: never sleeps
08-05.line: he that keepeth Israel doth neither slumber nor sleep.
08-05.meaning: you can rest. someone is keeping watch.

08-06.title: derech eretz
08-06.line: derech eretz: the way of the land, good manners.
08-06.meaning: the sages said manners come before Torah.

08-07.title: prayer is a plea
08-07.line: do not make your prayer routine, but a plea for mercy.
08-07.meaning: Rabbi Shimon: say it like you mean it, even if the words are the same.

08-08.title: sow in tears
08-08.line: they that sow in tears shall reap in joy.
08-08.meaning: hard seasons plant something. the harvest may surprise you.

08-09.title: caring for the body
08-09.line: washing is a mitzvah: the body is an image of God.
08-09.meaning: Hillel told his students he was off to do a mitzvah: the bathhouse.

08-10.title: rise for the old
08-10.line: thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man.
08-10.meaning: respect for elders is written right into the Torah.

08-11.title: a watered garden
08-11.line: thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.
08-11.meaning: a promise for dry seasons: you can be green again.

08-12.title: no gloating
08-12.line: rejoice not when thine enemy falleth.
08-12.meaning: even on a winning day, stay kind.

08-13.title: shalom bayit
08-13.line: shalom bayit: peace in the home.
08-13.meaning: sometimes keeping peace means choosing a softer word.

08-14.title: like dreamers
08-14.line: we were like unto them that dream.
08-14.meaning: sung before grace on Shabbat and holidays. sometimes good news feels too good to be real.

08-15.title: why the letter bet
08-15.line: the Torah opens with bet, closed on three sides and open forward.
08-15.meaning: the midrash says: don't obsess over what's before or above. look ahead.

08-16.title: love the stranger
08-16.line: the stranger... thou shalt love him as thyself.
08-16.meaning: the Torah asks this many times. it must matter a lot.

08-17.title: who builds the house
08-17.line: except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it.
08-17.meaning: work hard, and remember you're not building alone.

08-18.title: where are you going?
08-18.line: know from where you came, where you are going, and before whom you will give account.
08-18.meaning: Akavya's three questions keep life in perspective.

08-19.title: bikur cholim
08-19.meaning: a visit or call to someone unwell is a mitzvah.

08-20.title: holy, holy, holy
08-20.line: holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.
08-20.meaning: said standing, on tiptoe, in the Kedushah. the whole earth, including your street.

08-21.title: fitly spoken
08-21.line: a word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
08-21.meaning: the right word at the right time is a real gift.

08-22.title: your own two hands
08-22.line: when thou eatest the labour of thy hands, happy shalt thou be.
08-22.meaning: there's quiet joy in a meal you worked for. savor one today.

08-23.title: the highest giving
08-23.line: the highest form of tzedakah is helping someone stand on their own.
08-23.meaning: Maimonides' ladder of giving tops out with a job, a loan, a partnership.
08-23.source: Maimonides, Mishneh Torah, Gifts to the Poor 10:7

08-24.title: hachnasat orchim
08-24.meaning: an extra plate is a Jewish tradition as old as Abraham.

08-25.title: no hidden hate
08-25.line: thou shalt not hate thy brother in thy heart.
08-25.meaning: say it gently instead of storing it.

08-26.title: out of the depths
08-26.line: out of the depths have i called thee, O LORD.
08-26.meaning: you can pray from the bottom. the psalm started there too.

08-27.title: beloved
08-27.line: beloved is a person, for they were created in the image of God.
08-27.meaning: Rabbi Akiva: we're loved, and we're told we're loved. that's twice the gift.

08-28.title: quiet confidence
08-28.line: in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength.

08-29.title: feed your enemy
08-29.line: if thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat.
08-29.meaning: kindness can surprise even the people who expect it least.

08-30.title: give with a kind face
08-30.line: give with a pleasant face and with joy.
08-30.meaning: how you give matters as much as what you give.
08-30.source: Maimonides, Mishneh Torah, Gifts to the Poor 10:4 (paraphrase)

08-31.title: shmirat halashon
08-31.meaning: one gossip-free day is a real practice. try it.

09-01.title: a calm soul
09-01.line: like a weaned child with his mother, my soul is with me.
09-01.meaning: a picture of calm: not grasping, just resting close.

09-02.title: peace upon you
09-02.line: the LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.
09-02.meaning: the last words of the priestly blessing end with shalom.

09-03.title: together
09-03.line: how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
09-03.meaning: the song Hinei Ma Tov comes from here. call someone you miss.

09-04.title: arise, shine
09-04.line: arise, shine, for thy light is come.
09-04.meaning: Lecha Dodi on Friday night borrows these words. your light has arrived.

09-05.title: who is wise?
09-05.line: who is wise? one who learns from every person.
09-05.meaning: Ben Zoma: everyone you meet can teach you something.

09-06.title: anavah
09-06.meaning: Moses was called the humblest person on earth. humility makes room for others.

09-07.title: half and half
09-07.line: see yourself, and the world, as perfectly balanced: your next deed can tip the scale.
09-07.meaning: one good act today could tip everything.
09-07.source: Maimonides, Mishneh Torah, Laws of Repentance 3:4 (paraphrase)

09-08.title: iron sharpens iron
09-08.line: iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
09-08.meaning: good friends make each other sharper. that's why Jews traditionally study in pairs.

09-09.title: kindness forever
09-09.line: o give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever.
09-09.meaning: the psalm repeats 'his kindness endures forever' 26 times. some things are worth saying again.

09-10.title: everyone a prophet
09-10.line: would that all the LORD's people were prophets.
09-10.meaning: Moses wasn't jealous. he wished everyone could hear God.

09-11.title: emunah
09-11.meaning: the word is related to 'amen': something firm you can lean on.

09-12.title: as the waters
09-12.line: the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
09-12.meaning: a dream of a world full of wisdom, wall to wall.

09-13.title: wonderfully made
09-13.line: i am fearfully and wonderfully made.
09-13.meaning: you are part of the wonder, not just a witness to it.

09-14.title: the middle path
09-14.line: the right way is the middle path.
09-14.meaning: not too much, not too little. balance is a spiritual practice.
09-14.source: Maimonides, Mishneh Torah, Laws of Character 1:4 (paraphrase)

09-15.title: who is strong?
09-15.line: who is strong? one who masters their own impulses.
09-15.meaning: the strongest move is often the one you don't make.

09-16.title: face to face
09-16.line: as in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.
09-16.meaning: meet someone with warmth, and warmth usually comes back.

09-17.title: the fringes
09-17.line: that ye may look upon it, and remember all the commandments.
09-17.meaning: tzitzit are reminders you can touch. what helps you remember what matters?

09-18.title: amen
09-18.meaning: saying amen to someone's blessing is joining it.

09-19.title: wings of the morning
09-19.line: if i take the wings of the morning... even there shall thy hand lead me.
09-19.meaning: however far you go today, you aren't out of reach.

09-20.title: real return
09-20.line: full teshuvah: the same moment comes again, and you choose differently.
09-20.meaning: change shows up when the old situation returns.
09-20.source: Maimonides, Mishneh Torah, Laws of Repentance 2:1 (paraphrase)

09-21.title: not forgotten
09-21.line: can a woman forget her sucking child... yet will not i forget thee.
09-21.meaning: you are remembered with a parent's love.

09-22.title: good to all
09-22.line: the LORD is good to all; and his tender mercies are over all his works.
09-22.meaning: all means all. that includes the people you find hard today.

09-23.title: baruch hashem
09-23.meaning: the everyday answer to 'how are you?' gratitude in two words.

09-24.title: who is rich?
09-24.line: who is rich? one who is happy with their portion.
09-24.meaning: enough, noticed, is a kind of wealth.

09-25.title: tell your grandchildren
09-25.line: make them known unto thy children and thy children's children.
09-25.meaning: stories survive when they're told. share one today.

09-26.title: today, not tomorrow
09-26.line: boast not thyself of to-morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
09-26.meaning: today is the day you actually have.

09-27.title: an open hand
09-27.line: thou openest thy hand, and satisfiest every living thing with favour.
09-27.meaning: said in Ashrei, often while touching the tefillin. an open hand is how God is pictured feeding the world.

09-28.title: always joyful
09-28.line: it is a great mitzvah to be happy always.
09-28.meaning: Rabbi Nachman knew sadness well, and still taught this. joy can be chosen, a little at a time.
09-28.source: Rabbi Nachman of Breslov, Likutei Moharan II:24

09-29.title: what is asked
09-29.line: do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with thy God.
09-29.meaning: the whole of religion in three steps. pick one for today.

09-30.title: yasher koach
09-30.line: yasher koach: more strength to you.
09-30.meaning: said after someone does something good. hand one out today.

10-01.title: near to all who call
10-01.line: the LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon him in truth.
10-01.meaning: no special words needed. honest ones are enough.

10-02.title: all your heart
10-02.line: thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul.
10-02.meaning: the line right after the Shema. love with everything you are, and everything you have.

10-03.title: who is honored?
10-03.line: who is honored? one who honors others.
10-03.meaning: honor grows by giving it away.

10-04.title: a narrow bridge
10-04.line: the whole world is a very narrow bridge; the main thing is not to be afraid.
10-04.meaning: the famous song comes from this teaching. walk the bridge one step at a time.
10-04.source: Rabbi Nachman of Breslov, Likutei Moharan II:48 (paraphrase)

10-05.title: lifts the fallen
10-05.line: the LORD upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that are bowed down.
10-05.meaning: falling is part of being human. so is being lifted.

10-06.title: mazal tov
10-06.meaning: celebrating someone else's good news is a mitzvah too.

10-07.title: the near neighbor
10-07.line: better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.
10-07.meaning: say hello to someone next door today.

10-08.title: vine and fig tree
10-08.line: they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig-tree.
10-08.meaning: a picture of peace: enough, shade, no fear.

10-09.title: binds up wounds
10-09.line: he healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
10-09.meaning: the same God who counts the stars, the next verse says, cares about one hurting heart.

10-10.title: teach them
10-10.line: thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children... when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.
10-10.meaning: faith passed on at bedtime and breakfast, not just in class.

10-11.title: comforting mourners
10-11.line: 'may the Place comfort you among the mourners of Zion and Jerusalem.'
10-11.meaning: the traditional words to a mourner. showing up says more than any speech.

10-12.title: you can repair
10-12.line: if you believe you can damage, believe you can repair.
10-12.meaning: whatever broke, fixing is possible too.
10-12.source: Rabbi Nachman of Breslov, Likutei Moharan II:112 (paraphrase)

10-13.title: one good deed leads on
10-13.meaning: Ben Azzai: good deeds have momentum. start one.

10-14.title: stars by name
10-14.line: he counteth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by their names.
10-14.meaning: if every star has a name, so do you. you are known.

10-15.title: enough
10-15.line: give me neither poverty nor riches.
10-15.meaning: an old prayer for enough: not too little, not too much.

10-16.title: by my spirit
10-16.line: not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.
10-16.meaning: read on Shabbat of Hanukkah. the biggest changes aren't always loud.

10-17.title: of blessed memory
10-17.line: zichrono livracha: may his memory be a blessing.
10-17.meaning: said after naming someone who has died. their goodness keeps blessing us.

10-18.title: on the doorposts
10-18.line: thou shalt write them upon the door-posts of thy house.
10-18.meaning: that's the mezuzah: a blessing every time you walk through a door.

10-19.title: talk it out alone
10-19.line: speak to God in your own words, as to a friend.
10-19.meaning: hitbodedut: a few minutes of private, honest talk. try it on a walk.
10-19.source: Rabbi Nachman of Breslov, Likutei Moharan II:25 (paraphrase)

10-20.title: sun and moon
10-20.line: praise ye him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars of light.
10-20.meaning: the whole sky joins the morning prayers. you can too.

10-21.title: everyone has their hour
10-21.line: there is no person without their hour, and no thing without its place.
10-21.meaning: don't write anyone off. their moment may be coming.

10-22.title: every breath
10-22.line: let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD.
10-22.meaning: the last line of the Psalms. every breath you take today counts as a little praise.

10-23.title: speak truth
10-23.line: speak ye every man the truth with his neighbour.
10-23.meaning: honest and kind can go together. try both today.

10-24.title: oseh shalom
10-24.line: may the one who makes peace above make peace for us.
10-24.meaning: the closing line of the Kaddish and the Amidah. three steps back, then peace.

10-25.title: woman of valor
10-25.line: a woman of valour who can find?
10-25.meaning: sung at many Shabbat tables on Friday night, honoring the women who hold a home together.

10-26.title: be zusya
10-26.line: they won't ask me why i wasn't Moses. they'll ask why i wasn't Zusya.
10-26.meaning: Reb Zusya's worry, and comfort: you only have to be fully you.
10-26.source: attributed to Reb Zusya of Hanipol

10-27.title: love the stranger too
10-27.line: love ye therefore the stranger; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.

10-28.title: what is a person?
10-28.line: when i behold thy heavens, the work of thy fingers... what is man?
10-28.meaning: small under the sky, and still remembered. both are true.

10-29.title: ashrei three times
10-29.line: whoever says Ashrei three times a day is assured of a share in the world to come.
10-29.meaning: the sages loved Psalm 145 that much. it's an alphabet of praise.

10-30.title: a still small voice
10-30.line: after the fire a still small voice.
10-30.meaning: Elijah found God not in the wind or the quake, but in a quiet voice.

10-31.title: very humble
10-31.meaning: Levitas of Yavneh said 'very' twice. humility is worth doubling.

11-01.title: as the deer
11-01.line: as the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee.
11-01.meaning: longing is not a problem to fix. it's a sign you're alive to something bigger.

11-02.title: two pockets
11-02.line: in one pocket: 'i am dust and ashes.' in the other: 'the world was created for me.'
11-02.meaning: Rabbi Simcha Bunim said to reach for whichever note you need today.
11-02.source: attributed to Rabbi Simcha Bunim of Peshischa

11-03.title: a kind tongue
11-03.line: she openeth her mouth with wisdom; and the law of kindness is on her tongue.
11-03.meaning: the Hebrew is torat chesed, a teaching of kindness. let it set your tone today.

11-04.title: rejoice in your festival
11-04.line: thou shalt rejoice in thy feast.
11-04.meaning: joy is a commandment. that's a nice rule to have.

11-05.title: the minyan
11-05.meaning: some prayers need a group. you're part of something bigger.

11-06.title: hope again
11-06.line: why art thou cast down, O my soul? hope thou in God.
11-06.meaning: the psalmist talks to their own sad soul, gently. you can do that too.

11-07.title: like water
11-07.line: let justice well up as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.
11-07.meaning: justice that keeps flowing, not a one-time splash.

11-08.title: where is god?
11-08.meaning: the Kotzker Rebbe's answer to a famous question.

11-09.title: the jug and the wine
11-09.line: do not look at the jug, but at what is in it.
11-09.meaning: Rabbi Meir: new jugs can hold old wine. don't judge by the outside.

11-10.title: light in light
11-10.line: in thy light do we see light.
11-10.meaning: some things only become clear when you see them in a kinder light.

11-11.title: grace after meals
11-11.line: you will eat, be satisfied, and bless.
11-11.meaning: birkat hamazon comes after eating, when you're full. gratitude when you have enough.

11-12.title: spare the trees
11-12.line: thou shalt not destroy the trees thereof.
11-12.meaning: from this verse the sages taught bal tashchit: don't waste what the world gives.

11-13.title: an open hand
11-13.line: she stretcheth out her hand to the poor.
11-13.meaning: part of the Eishet Chayil song: valor includes generosity.

11-14.title: truth and kindness meet
11-14.line: mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
11-14.meaning: kindness and honesty don't have to fight. today they can hold hands.

11-15.title: their needs, my soul
11-15.line: another person's material needs are my spiritual needs.
11-15.meaning: feeding someone can be as holy as praying.

11-16.title: the tallit
11-16.line: a prayer shawl with fringes at the corners.
11-16.meaning: wrapped in the tallit, many feel held while they pray.

11-17.title: one father
11-17.line: have we not all one father? hath not one God created us?
11-17.meaning: every person you meet today is family, in a deep way.

11-18.title: not in heaven
11-18.meaning: the Torah is close and doable, not out of reach.

11-19.title: built with kindness
11-19.line: the world is built with kindness.
11-19.meaning: the Hebrew is olam chesed yibaneh. every kind act today is a brick in the world.

11-20.title: timing kindness
11-20.line: do not comfort your friend while his dead lies before him.
11-20.meaning: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar: sometimes presence beats words. just be there.

11-21.title: laughing at tomorrow
11-21.line: strength and dignity are her clothing; and she laugheth at the time to come.
11-21.meaning: the hope of meeting the future with a smile, not dread.

11-22.title: adon olam
11-22.line: into his hand i entrust my spirit, when i sleep and when i wake.
11-22.meaning: from the hymn Adon Olam, sung at the end of services. a calm close.

11-23.title: old made new
11-23.line: the old shall be renewed, and the new shall be made holy.
11-23.meaning: Rav Kook's hope: honor tradition, welcome what's new.
11-23.source: attributed to Rabbi Abraham Isaac Kook

11-24.title: a tree by water
11-24.line: like a tree planted by streams of water, that bringeth forth its fruit in its season.
11-24.meaning: the first psalm's picture of a good life: rooted, watered, patient.

11-25.title: kindness, not ritual
11-25.line: for i desire mercy, and not sacrifice.
11-25.meaning: rituals matter, and kindness matters more.

11-26.title: strong and brave
11-26.line: be strong and of good courage, fear not.
11-26.meaning: said to a whole people before a new chapter. it fits yours too.

11-27.title: sleep in peace
11-27.line: in peace will i both lay me down and sleep.
11-27.meaning: a line for tonight. let the day go and rest.

11-28.title: lecha dodi
11-28.line: come, my beloved, to greet the bride.
11-28.meaning: on Friday night the congregation turns to the door to welcome Shabbat.

11-29.title: love without conditions
11-29.line: love that does not depend on anything will never end.
11-29.meaning: like David and Jonathan, whose friendship needed nothing in return.

11-30.title: wiser still
11-30.line: give to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser.
11-30.meaning: wise people love learning more. stay curious today.

12-01.title: a palace in time
12-01.line: Shabbat is a palace built in time, not space.
12-01.meaning: Rabbi Abraham Joshua Heschel's idea: holiness can live in hours, not just places.

12-02.title: stillness
12-02.line: only for God doth my soul wait in stillness.
12-02.meaning: waiting can be quiet and trusting, not anxious. try it for one breath.

12-03.title: roots by water
12-03.line: as a tree planted by the waters, that spreadeth out its roots by the river.
12-03.meaning: deep roots make for calm in dry years.

12-04.title: never forsaken
12-04.line: he will not fail thee, neither forsake thee.
12-04.meaning: a promise to keep in your pocket.

12-05.title: aleinu
12-05.line: it is upon us to praise.
12-05.meaning: the Aleinu ends almost every service. a hope that the world will be made whole.

12-06.title: radical amazement
12-06.line: wonder is the start of faith.
12-06.meaning: Heschel taught that amazement, not answers, opens the heart.
12-06.source: Abraham Joshua Heschel, God in Search of Man (paraphrase)

12-07.title: in old age
12-07.line: cast me not off in the time of old age.
12-07.meaning: a prayer from Yom Kippur. call an older person you love today.

12-08.title: arguments that last
12-08.line: every argument for the sake of heaven will endure.
12-08.meaning: like Hillel and Shammai: they disagreed for truth, not to win.

12-09.title: mother's teaching
12-09.line: hear, my son, the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the teaching of thy mother.
12-09.meaning: the word for teaching here is torah. parents are the first teachers.

12-10.title: rest is holy
12-10.line: on Shabbat, even the animals rest.
12-10.meaning: the Torah includes workers and animals in Shabbat rest. rest is for everyone.

12-11.title: the old paths
12-11.line: ask for the old paths... and ye shall find rest for your souls.
12-11.meaning: old wisdom can still bring new rest.

12-12.title: nearness
12-12.line: but as for me, the nearness of God is my good.
12-12.meaning: after a whole psalm of questions, the answer is simple: closeness.

12-13.title: ask your elders
12-13.line: ask thy father, and he will declare unto thee; thine elders, and they will tell thee.
12-13.meaning: there's wisdom in the people who came before you. ask them a question.

12-14.title: gathering sparks
12-14.line: holy sparks are scattered everywhere, waiting to be lifted.
12-14.meaning: in the teaching of Rabbi Isaac Luria, every good act lifts a spark back to its source.

12-15.title: a whole heart
12-15.line: teach me thy way, O LORD... unite my heart to fear thy name.
12-15.meaning: a pulled-apart heart can ask to be made whole.

12-16.title: the shabbat greeting
12-16.meaning: two words that mean: may your rest be peaceful and whole.

12-17.title: turn it and turn it
12-17.line: turn it and turn it, for everything is in it.
12-17.meaning: Ben Bag Bag on the Torah: keep looking. there's always more.

12-18.title: walk with the wise
12-18.line: he that walketh with wise men shall be wise.
12-18.meaning: who you spend time with shapes who you become.

12-19.title: dreams and visions
12-19.line: your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions.
12-19.meaning: every age has its own way of hoping.

12-20.title: everlasting arms
12-20.meaning: when everything feels unsteady, something holds you from below.

12-21.title: how can i repay
12-21.line: how can i repay unto the LORD all his bountiful dealings toward me?
12-21.meaning: the answer the psalm gives: lift a cup and call out thanks.

12-22.title: making room
12-22.line: God drew back to make room for the world.
12-22.meaning: tzimtzum: sometimes love means making space for someone else.

12-23.title: good week
12-23.line: shavua tov: have a good week.
12-23.meaning: said after Havdalah, when Shabbat ends. a fresh start every Saturday night.

12-24.title: the rejected stone
12-24.line: the stone which the builders rejected is become the chief corner-stone.
12-24.meaning: what others overlooked can end up holding everything together. including you.

12-25.title: effort counts
12-25.line: according to the effort is the reward.
12-25.meaning: Ben Hei Hei: the trying itself counts.

12-26.title: commit your works
12-26.line: commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.
12-26.meaning: offer today's work up, and your thoughts often settle.

12-27.title: joy is strength
12-27.line: the joy of the LORD is your strength.
12-27.meaning: Nehemiah tells a crying crowd to go eat, share, and be glad. joy is fuel.

12-28.title: bless your children
12-28.line: God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh.
12-28.meaning: many parents bless their children with these words on Friday night, hands on their heads.

12-29.title: days are scrolls
12-29.line: your days are scrolls: write on them what you want remembered.
12-29.meaning: a line often traced to Bahya ibn Paquda. what will today's page say?
12-29.source: attributed to Bahya ibn Paquda, Duties of the Heart (paraphrase)

12-30.title: good morning, in prayer
12-30.line: how good are your tents, O Jacob.
12-30.meaning: Mah Tovu, often the first line said on entering a synagogue.

12-31.title: open my lips
12-31.line: o Lord, open thou my lips; and my mouth shall declare thy praise.
12-31.meaning: the quiet first words of the Amidah. sometimes we need help even to begin.

2026-10-17.title: Parashat Noach
2026-10-17.line: i have set my bow in the cloud.
2026-10-17.meaning: after the flood, the rainbow is a promise: no matter how big the storm, the world goes on.

2026-10-24.title: Parashat Lech Lecha
2026-10-24.line: get thee out of thy country... unto the land that i will show thee.
2026-10-24.meaning: lech lecha can be read 'go to yourself.' every journey out is also a journey in.

2026-10-31.title: Parashat Vayera
2026-10-31.line: he ran to meet them from the tent door.
2026-10-31.meaning: Abraham, recovering in the heat, still runs to welcome three strangers. hospitality at its warmest.

2026-11-07.title: Parashat Chayei Sara
2026-11-07.line: Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide.
2026-11-07.meaning: the sages say this is where the afternoon prayer began: a walk in a field at dusk.

2026-11-11.title: Kislev begins
2026-11-11.line: Kislev is the month of Hanukkah.
2026-11-11.meaning: the nights are getting longer. the lights are coming.

2026-11-14.title: Parashat Toldot
2026-11-14.line: the voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
2026-11-14.meaning: a story about pretending to be someone else. this week, try being fully yourself.

2026-11-21.title: Parashat Vayetzei
2026-11-21.line: surely the LORD is in this place; and i knew it not.
2026-11-21.meaning: Jacob wakes from his ladder dream amazed. the holy was there all along.

2026-11-28.title: Parashat Vayishlach
2026-11-28.line: and Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him... and they wept.
2026-11-28.meaning: after twenty years apart, two brothers hug. reconciliation can still happen.

2026-12-04.title: the first candle
2026-12-04.line: blessed are you... who performed miracles for our ancestors in those days, at this season.
2026-12-04.meaning: Hanukkah begins tonight. it's Friday, so light the menorah first, then the Shabbat candles.

2026-12-05.title: a great miracle
2026-12-05.meaning: the four letters on a dreidel. tonight, light two candles after Shabbat ends. this Shabbat's portion is Vayeshev, Joseph's dreams.

2026-12-06.title: the helper candle
2026-12-06.line: the helper candle lights all the others.
2026-12-06.meaning: the shamash stands a little apart and shares its flame. that's a kind of greatness.

2026-12-07.title: going up
2026-12-07.line: in holiness we go up, not down.
2026-12-07.meaning: Hillel's school added a candle each night instead of taking one away. let good things grow.

2026-12-08.title: in the window
2026-12-08.line: place the light where the street can see it.
2026-12-08.meaning: the menorah goes in a window or doorway to share the miracle with passersby.

2026-12-09.title: only to look at
2026-12-09.line: these lights are holy; we may only look at them.
2026-12-09.meaning: from Haneirot Halalu: the candles aren't for reading by. just for seeing and thanking.

2026-12-10.title: rock of ages
2026-12-10.line: Maoz Tzur: rock of my salvation, to praise you is a delight.
2026-12-10.meaning: the song sung after lighting. it tells of rescue after rescue.

2026-12-11.title: enough for eight
2026-12-11.line: one small jar of oil, enough for one day, lasted eight.
2026-12-11.meaning: all eight candles tonight. it's Friday, so light the menorah before the Shabbat candles.

2026-12-12.title: zot hanukkah
2026-12-12.line: it is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.
2026-12-12.meaning: the last day of Hanukkah, and Shabbat Miketz. Joseph doesn't take credit for his gift. quiet humility, like a small flame.

2026-12-19.title: Parashat Vayigash
2026-12-19.line: i am Joseph; doth my father yet live?
2026-12-19.meaning: Joseph stops hiding and tells the truth. the first thing he asks about is his father.

2026-12-20.title: a fast day
2026-12-20.line: therefore love ye truth and peace.
2026-12-20.meaning: a dawn-to-dusk fast remembering the siege of Jerusalem. the prophet promised these fasts would one day become feasts.

2026-12-26.title: Parashat Vayechi
2026-12-26.line: ye meant evil against me; but God meant it for good.
2026-12-26.meaning: Joseph forgives his brothers. the book of Genesis ends with mercy. chazak, chazak: be strong.

2027-01-02.title: Parashat Shemot
2027-01-02.line: i will turn aside now, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.
2027-01-02.meaning: Moses noticed a small wonder and stopped to look. that's when everything changed.

2027-01-09.title: Parashat Vaera
2027-01-09.line: they hearkened not unto Moses for impatience of spirit, and for cruel bondage.
2027-01-09.meaning: people who are crushed can't always hear hope. be gentle with anyone short of breath.

2027-01-16.title: Parashat Bo
2027-01-16.line: all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.
2027-01-16.meaning: in the plague of darkness, homes still had light. may yours this week.

2027-01-23.title: the new year for trees
2027-01-23.line: the LORD is my strength and song.
2027-01-23.meaning: two joys today: the birthday of the trees, and the Song at the Sea. eat a fruit you haven't tasted this season.

2027-01-30.title: Parashat Yitro
2027-01-30.line: the thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.
2027-01-30.meaning: Moses' father-in-law tells him to share the load. the week of the Ten Commandments begins with delegating.

2027-02-06.title: Parashat Mishpatim
2027-02-06.line: all that the LORD hath spoken will we do, and we will hear.
2027-02-06.meaning: na'aseh v'nishma: sometimes you understand by doing first.

2027-02-08.title: Adar begins
2027-02-08.meaning: this is a leap year, so there are two Adars. some say: double the joy.

2027-02-13.title: Parashat Terumah
2027-02-13.line: let them make me a sanctuary, that i may dwell among them.
2027-02-13.meaning: the sages noticed it says 'among them,' not 'in it.' God dwells in people.

2027-02-20.title: Parashat Tetzaveh
2027-02-20.line: pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually.
2027-02-20.meaning: the ner tamid, the eternal light over the ark, comes from here. keep a small light burning.

2027-02-27.title: Parashat Ki Tisa
2027-02-27.line: the LORD, the LORD, God, merciful and gracious, long-suffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.
2027-02-27.meaning: after the golden calf, God's thirteen attributes of mercy. a second chance is built in.

2027-03-06.title: Parashat Vayakhel
2027-03-06.line: every one whose heart stirred him up, and every one whom his spirit made willing.
2027-03-06.meaning: the Tabernacle was built by willing hearts. it's also Shabbat Shekalim, when everyone gave the same half-shekel.

2027-03-10.title: second Adar begins
2027-03-10.line: a leap year gives us a whole extra month.
2027-03-10.meaning: the Hebrew calendar adds a month to stay in step with spring. Purim falls this month.

2027-03-13.title: Parashat Pekudei
2027-03-13.line: the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
2027-03-13.meaning: the work is finished and filled with presence. the book of Exodus ends: chazak, chazak, v'nitchazek.

2027-03-20.title: Parashat Vayikra
2027-03-20.line: and the LORD called unto Moses.
2027-03-20.meaning: the first word is written with a small aleph, a sign of Moses' humility. it's also Shabbat Zachor, before Purim.

2027-03-22.title: for such a time
2027-03-22.line: who knoweth whether thou art not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
2027-03-22.meaning: Esther fasted before taking her big risk. tonight, Purim begins with the reading of the Megillah.

2027-03-23.title: the day of gladness
2027-03-23.line: days of feasting and gladness, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.
2027-03-23.meaning: Purim's four mitzvot: hear the Megillah, share food with friends, give to the poor, and feast.

2027-03-24.title: light and gladness
2027-03-24.line: the Jews had light and gladness, and joy and honour.
2027-03-24.meaning: in walled cities like Jerusalem, Purim is celebrated today. this verse is also said every week at Havdalah.

2027-03-27.title: Parashat Tzav
2027-03-27.line: fire shall be kept burning upon the altar continually; it shall not go out.
2027-03-27.meaning: a steady flame, tended daily. it's also Shabbat Parah, preparing for Passover.

2027-04-03.title: Parashat Shmini
2027-04-03.meaning: in deep grief, Aaron is silent. sometimes silence is the most honest answer. it's also Shabbat HaChodesh: Nisan is near.

2027-04-08.title: Nisan begins
2027-04-08.line: this month shall be unto you the beginning of months.
2027-04-08.meaning: the month of Passover and spring. many say a blessing on seeing fruit trees in bloom.

2027-04-10.title: Parashat Tazria
2027-04-10.meaning: a hard verse with a kind reading: the sages taught the call let others know to pray for the person.

2027-04-17.title: Parashat Metzora
2027-04-17.line: he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children.
2027-04-17.meaning: the portion is about healing and coming home. today is Shabbat HaGadol, the great Shabbat before Passover.
2027-04-17.source: Leviticus 14:1-15:33; line from Malachi 3:24 (haftarah of Shabbat HaGadol)

2027-04-21.title: the first seder
2027-04-21.line: this is the bread of affliction... let all who are hungry come and eat.
2027-04-21.meaning: the seder opens by inviting everyone in. tonight is the first night of Passover.

2027-04-22.title: as if you were there
2027-04-22.line: in every generation, each person must see themselves as if they went out of Egypt.
2027-04-22.meaning: freedom is personal. tonight is the second seder, and the counting of the Omer begins.

2027-04-23.title: tell your children
2027-04-23.line: and thou shalt tell thy son in that day.
2027-04-23.meaning: the whole seder grows from this verse. the story lives when it's told.

2027-04-24.title: a seal on the heart
2027-04-24.line: set me as a seal upon thy heart.
2027-04-24.meaning: the Song of Songs is read on the Shabbat of Passover: spring, love, and freedom.

2027-04-25.title: dayenu
2027-04-25.meaning: the seder song counts gifts one by one. try your own dayenu list today.

2027-04-26.title: nothing puffed up
2027-04-26.line: matzah is only flour and water: nothing puffed up.
2027-04-26.meaning: a Hasidic reading: this week, let go of a little pride along with the bread.

2027-04-27.title: four children
2027-04-27.line: speak to each child in their own way.
2027-04-27.meaning: the Haggadah's four children each get a different answer. people learn differently.

2027-04-28.title: dry land in the sea
2027-04-28.line: the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the midst of the sea.
2027-04-28.meaning: the day the sea split. the midrash says Nachshon stepped in first, before it opened.

2027-04-29.title: the wolf and the lamb
2027-04-29.line: the wolf shall dwell with the lamb.
2027-04-29.meaning: the last day of Passover reads Isaiah's dream of a peaceful world. Yizkor, the memorial prayer, is said today.
2027-04-29.source: Isaiah 11:6 (the eighth day is kept outside Israel)

2027-05-01.title: Parashat Achrei Mot
2027-05-01.line: which if a man do, he shall live by them.
2027-05-01.meaning: the sages read it: live by the commandments, not die by them. life comes first.

2027-05-04.title: to remember
2027-05-04.line: light a candle, and say a name.
2027-05-04.meaning: today Jews remember the six million murdered in the Holocaust. remembering is an act of love.

2027-05-08.title: Parashat Kedoshim
2027-05-08.line: thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
2027-05-08.meaning: Rabbi Akiva called this a great principle of the Torah. it sits in a chapter about ordinary holiness.

2027-05-15.title: Parashat Emor
2027-05-15.line: thou shalt not wholly reap the corner of thy field... leave them for the poor.
2027-05-15.meaning: right in the middle of the holidays, a reminder: leave something for others.

2027-05-22.title: Parashat Behar
2027-05-22.line: proclaim liberty throughout the land unto all the inhabitants thereof.
2027-05-22.meaning: the Jubilee: every fifty years, a reset. fresh starts are built into the Torah.

2027-05-25.title: the 33rd day
2027-05-25.line: Rabbi Akiva's students did not treat one another with respect.
2027-05-25.meaning: the sages tied the mourning of the Omer to this. Lag BaOmer is a day of joy, bonfires, and picnics.

2027-05-29.title: Parashat Bechukotai
2027-05-29.line: ye shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid.
2027-05-29.meaning: the blessing of peace: sleeping without fear. Leviticus ends: chazak, chazak, v'nitchazek.

2027-06-05.title: Parashat Bamidbar
2027-06-05.line: take ye the sum of all the congregation... by their names.
2027-06-05.meaning: everyone is counted, by name. read just before Shavuot: each of us stood at Sinai.

2027-06-06.title: Sivan begins
2027-06-06.line: Sivan brings Shavuot, the giving of the Torah.
2027-06-06.meaning: in a few days, the gift at Sinai is celebrated again.

2027-06-10.title: a night of learning
2027-06-10.line: tonight, many stay up until dawn learning Torah.
2027-06-10.meaning: Shavuot marks the giving of the Torah. the all-night study is like getting ready for a wedding.

2027-06-11.title: at sinai
2027-06-11.line: i am the LORD thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt.
2027-06-11.meaning: the Ten Commandments are read today. the midrash says each person heard them in a way they could hold.

2027-06-12.title: the book of ruth
2027-06-12.line: the LORD deal kindly with you, as ye have dealt with the dead, and with me.
2027-06-12.meaning: Ruth is read on Shavuot. the sages said it was written to teach the reward of kindness. Yizkor is said today.
2027-06-12.source: Ruth 1:8 (second day is kept outside Israel)

2027-06-19.title: Parashat Nasso
2027-06-19.line: the LORD bless thee, and keep thee.
2027-06-19.meaning: the priestly blessing, said by parents to children and by the kohanim in synagogue.
2027-06-19.source: Numbers 4:21-7:89; line from Numbers 6:24 (outside Israel; Israel reads a week ahead)

2027-06-26.title: Parashat Beha'alotcha
2027-06-26.line: heal her now, O God, i beseech thee.
2027-06-26.meaning: Moses prays for his sister Miriam in five Hebrew words. a short prayer can be enough.
2027-06-26.source: Numbers 8:1-12:16; line from Numbers 12:13 (outside Israel; Israel reads a week ahead)

2027-07-03.title: Parashat Sh'lach
2027-07-03.line: we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.
2027-07-03.meaning: how we see ourselves shapes how others see us. try seeing yourself kindly.
2027-07-03.source: Numbers 13:1-15:41; line from Numbers 13:33 (outside Israel; Israel reads a week ahead)

2027-07-06.title: Tammuz begins
2027-07-06.line: Tammuz is the heart of summer.
2027-07-06.meaning: long days, slow evenings. a good month to rest and read.

2027-07-10.title: Parashat Korach
2027-07-10.line: o God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin...?
2027-07-10.meaning: even in a rebellion against him, Moses pleads for the people.
2027-07-10.source: Numbers 16:1-18:32; line from Numbers 16:22 (outside Israel; Israel reads a week ahead)

2027-07-17.title: Parashat Chukat-Balak
2027-07-17.line: and Miriam died there... and there was no water for the congregation.
2027-07-17.meaning: the sages say a well followed Miriam in the desert. when she was gone, the water stopped. some people are wells.
2027-07-17.source: Numbers 19:1-25:9; line from Numbers 20:1-2 (outside Israel; Israel reads a week ahead)

2027-07-22.title: the three weeks begin
2027-07-22.line: turn thou us unto thee, O LORD... renew our days as of old.
2027-07-22.meaning: a fast day that begins three quieter weeks before Tisha B'Av.

2027-07-24.title: Parashat Pinchas
2027-07-24.line: the daughters of Zelophehad speak right.
2027-07-24.meaning: five sisters asked for fairness, and God agreed. speaking up can change the law.

2027-07-31.title: Parashat Matot-Masei
2027-07-31.line: these are the journeys of the children of Israel.
2027-07-31.meaning: every stop in the desert is listed. every stage of your journey counts too. Numbers ends: chazak.

2027-08-04.title: Av begins
2027-08-04.line: when Av begins, joy is lessened.
2027-08-04.meaning: nine quieter days lead to Tisha B'Av. then comes comfort, and Tu B'Av, a day of love.

2027-08-07.title: Parashat Devarim
2027-08-07.line: ye shall hear the small and the great alike.
2027-08-07.meaning: fairness means listening to everyone. today is Shabbat Chazon, before Tisha B'Av.

2027-08-11.title: eicha
2027-08-11.line: how doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people!
2027-08-11.meaning: tonight, Lamentations is read by low light, sitting on the floor. grief is given a place.

2027-08-12.title: from hatred to love
2027-08-12.line: the second Temple was destroyed because of baseless hatred.
